records.tips:
- Having gone through the PGDBA selection process this year, I thought I'd share a few suggestions for future aspirants. These are based entirely on what worked for me.
- For the Written Test:
- Start with Previous Year Questions (PYQs)—they give the best idea of the exam pattern and difficulty.
- Practice easy to medium JEE Mathematics questions to strengthen your fundamentals.
- If time permits, refer to TOMATO for additional practice.
- For the Interview:
- Be confident and be yourself. The interview is as much about your thought process as it is about your knowledge.
- Know your profile thoroughly—your birthplace, educational background, workplace, projects, hobbies, and stay updated with current affairs.
- "Why PGDBA?" is probably the most important question. Your answer should clearly explain your motivation and career goals, as it often sets the direction for the rest of the interview.
- Be able to tell your work experience as a concise story. Explain what you do, the business problems you solve, and how analytics fits into your work.
- Build a balanced understanding of Probability & Statistics, Calculus, Linear Algebra, and Machine Learning. If you have relevant experience, revise DSA as well.
- Finally, don't underestimate the importance of a good night's sleep before the interview. A fresh mind helps you think clearly and communicate confidently.
- Most importantly, don't try to know everything. Focus on understanding the fundamentals, think logically, and communicate your ideas clearly.
- Wishing the very best to everyone preparing for PGDBA!

records.tips:
- Score high in written, Interview can go sideways. My interview was terrible (atleast from my pov), idk how I got the call. Do PYPs in a timed fashion and aim for a 130+ score, time advantage will be there in exams if your fundamentals are strong
- For interview revise all of your undergrad properly, if you have relevant work experience the interview might revolve around that and you have scope to shape it towards where you want it to go. If not then the same old suggestion that everyone will give about Linear Algebra, Probability and Statistics.
- Don't Shy away from saying "No/I don't know" to questions. That is what I had said during my interview so many times. Better not fake the answers, they'll show you your place.
- I spent half my interview prep time just studying for the "Why PGDBA" question given my profile but they didn't probe
